name: Stir the Pot
description: Stir the pot is a Swiss ball core stability exercise developed by Dr. Stuart McGill in which the athlete maintains a plank position with forearms on the ball and moves the ball in circles, creating a combined anti-extension and anti-rotation core demand. The unstable surface of the ball dramatically increases muscle activation compared to a floor plank, while the circular motion forces the core to resist motion in multiple planes simultaneously. It is a highly effective anti-movement core exercise for athletes and advanced fitness populations.

execution.starting_position: Kneel behind a Swiss ball and place both forearms on the top of the ball, making fists or clasping hands. Walk the feet back until the body is in a straight plank line from head to feet.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a properly inflated Swiss ball sized for your height (55 cm for shorter individuals, 65 cm for average height, 75 cm for taller). Ensure the ball is on a non-slip surface.
steps: Step 1: Set up in the forearm plank position on the Swiss ball.
Step 2: Brace the entire core and ensure the body forms a straight line.
Step 3: Begin slowly rolling the ball in a small clockwise circle using the forearms.
Step 4: Keep the hips level and the lower back from sagging throughout each circle.
Step 5: Complete the prescribed number of circles in one direction, then reverse direction.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously throughout. Maintain the core brace without holding the breath.
common_mistakes: Allowing the hips to sag or pike during the circular motion
Making circles that are too large — start small and increase diameter as strength improves
Rotating the torso rather than keeping it rigid throughout
safety_considerations: Ensure the ball is on a non-slip surface to prevent it rolling away.
Regress to a standard forearm plank if unable to maintain spinal neutrality.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Start with small circles (20–30 cm diameter) and progress to larger circles as core strength improves.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2–3 seconds per circle. Perform 5–10 circles per direction per set.
